description: A small validator (PostalCodeValidator) and a masking utility (StringMasks), both with private empty constructors, fully tested with JUnit 5 parameterized tests, a @Nested class and fully-qualified @org.junit.jupiter.api.Test annotations. JaCoCo (pretty-printed) is exactly 100% on every counter. The scope is a plain list of fully-qualified class names, one per line, that matches the report classes exactly. Two Surefire XML pastes (one per test class) are all green and use display-name style testcase names ("[1] SG, 018956, true", "nullCountryIsInvalid()").
notes: strict100 is true; both classes have BRANCH counters (PostalCodeValidator 12 + StringMasks 6 = 18 branches), all covered.

The scope paste is a bare FQCN list (no paths), so changedFiles is empty and changedProductionClasses equals the set of <class> names in the report (with "/" -> "."). Every changed class is present in JaCoCo at 100%.

Both classes have private empty no-arg constructors, which JaCoCo filters: there is no <init> method for either class. StringMasks has no <clinit> because MASK is a compile-time char constant; PostalCodeValidator <clinit> covers the multi-line Map.of initialiser (lines 11-14).
Three PostalCodeValidatorTest methods use the fully-qualified annotation @org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and there is no import of org.junit.jupiter.api.Test in that file.

Surefire: 12 testcases for PostalCodeValidatorTest (7 validatesPerCountry + 2 unsupportedCountries + 3 plain) and 6 for StringMasksTest (3 masksAllButLast + nullStaysNull + 2 in the @Nested class, reported with classname com.acme.common.text.StringMasksTest$Email). Testcase names are display names (phrased reporter): plain tests end with "()", parameterized invocations start with "[n]" and do not contain the method name.

The second validatesPerCountry invocation name is "[2] sg,  018956 , true" because the quoted CSV value ' 018956 ' keeps its spaces. The StringMasksTest invocation names come from @ParameterizedTest(name = "[{index}] {0} keep {1} -> {2}") and contain "->" (escaped as -> in the XML).
Source Javadoc line 13 of StringMasks contains {@code visible} and an arrow example; the PostalCodeValidator regex literals contain {6}, {5}, {1,2} and {2} quantifiers.
